skill.name: database-migration
skill.description: Manage versioned database schema changes with Prisma, Drizzle, rollback planning, and production migration checks.
skill.summary: Guides safe, versioned database migrations for Prisma, Drizzle, CI validation, rollback planning, and production checks.
skill.author: Doyajin174

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from markdown code fences, ORM configuration examples, documentation links, and placeholder DATABASE_URL references. No prompt-injection text or credential exfiltration intent was found. The main residual risk is operational: migration deploy and reset workflows can modify or delete database data without careful approval.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation before running deploy, push, or reset commands, and verify the target database before execution.
Use neutral placeholders for connection strings and label local test URLs as non-production examples.
Require backup confirmation, generated SQL review, and rollback planning before production migration commands.

semantic_findings.title: Destructive Database Migration Commands
semantic_findings.description: The skill is legitimate, but it includes migration deploy and reset workflows that can alter or delete database data. These commands require explicit user approval and target database verification before execution.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines include prisma migrate deploy and reset guidance, including a CI production-style DATABASE_URL use. The file also recommends backups, so this is operational risk rather than malicious intent.

content.value_statement: Schema changes can break deployments when teams apply them manually. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through versioned Prisma and Drizzle migration workflows.
actual_capabilities: Guides Prisma setup, schema definitions, and migration commands.
Shows Drizzle schema configuration and drizzle-kit migration workflows.
Explains safer patterns for columns, indexes, rollbacks, and small migrations.
Provides CI examples for migration deployment and validation jobs.
Lists production checks before, during, and after database changes.
limitations: It provides guidance only and does not inspect a live database by itself.
Examples focus mainly on PostgreSQL, Prisma, Drizzle, and Node.js projects.
Migration commands can change or remove data when run against real databases.
Complex production migrations still need DBA or senior engineering review.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Project Schema
use_cases.description: Create versioned migrations before the first production deployment.

use_cases.title: Review a Migration Pull Request
use_cases.description: Check schema changes for rollback gaps, data-loss risks, and unsafe deployment order.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Production Release
use_cases.description: Build a migration checklist that covers backups, CI validation, monitoring, and rollback steps.

prompt_templates.title: Create First Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: I am starting a Node.js project with PostgreSQL. Help me set up versioned migrations with Prisma and a checklist before I run anything.

prompt_templates.title: Review Migration Safety
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this planned schema change: [describe change]. Identify data-loss risks, rollback needs, and safer rollout steps.

prompt_templates.title: Build CI Migration Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a CI workflow that validates database migrations on pull requests and applies approved migrations during deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Design Zero-Downtime Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a zero-downtime migration plan for [change] on a large PostgreSQL table. Include phases, backfill, validation, and rollback.

output_examples.input: Add a required user status field to an existing table.
output: Add the field as nullable or with a safe default first.
Backfill existing rows in a controlled step.
Validate application compatibility before enforcing the required constraint.

output_examples.input: Prepare a production migration pull request.
output_examples.output: The response lists migration files to review, backup checks, rollout order, monitoring points, and rollback actions.

output_examples.input: Move a large table to a new schema without downtime.
output_examples.output: The response separates schema creation, dual-write planning, backfill validation, read cutover, and delayed cleanup.

best_practices: Back up production data and verify rollback steps before running migrations.
Review generated SQL and test it against a disposable database first.
Keep each migration small and tied to one schema change.
anti_patterns: Running manual ALTER statements outside version control.
Running reset commands against shared or production databases.
Combining schema rewrites, data moves, and cleanup in one migration.

faq.question: Does this skill run migrations automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow guidance and command examples. Users should approve commands before execution.

faq.question: Which tools does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers Prisma, Drizzle ORM, PostgreSQL examples, and CI workflows for migration validation.

faq.question: Can it help with rollback planning?
faq.answer: Yes. It encourages rollback scripts, recovery points, and validation before production changes.

faq.question: Is it suitable for production databases?
faq.answer: Yes, but only with backups, review, staged rollout, monitoring, and explicit operator approval.

faq.question: Does it replace database administrator review?
faq.answer: No. High-risk or large-scale migrations still need expert review and environment-specific testing.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use it in a repository?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide repository changes and migration review when the user provides project context.
